phrase.zh: 连续的瞬间，留下时间的形状。
phrase.en: Successive moments give time a shape.

visual.zh: 胶片、镜头与人物侧影把电影呈现为时间的保存和重新编排。画面不是历史电影剧照，也不指认一段真实拍摄经历。
visual.en: Film, lenses and a profile present cinema as preserving and rearranging time. This is not a historical film still or a record of an actual shoot.

background.zh: 美国国家档案馆解释，电影胶片由一系列静态画格组成，通常以每秒 24 格播放时呈现运动。这里的“通常”很重要：不同历史时期和媒介并非都使用相同帧率。运动感来自画格的连续呈现，而单张胶片保存的是一个瞬间。
background.en: The US National Archives describes motion-picture film as successive still frames, usually projected at 24 frames per second to show motion. “Usually” matters: rates vary across eras and media. A single frame preserves one moment; motion emerges from their presentation in sequence.
